action_summary: The formatter was unreachable and unjudged, both halves of which were already in the tree. `ruff` had no entry in `_MUTATING_POSTCONDITIONS` (and none in the read-only table), so `_prose_argv` refused to translate the plainest sentence in the family: `extract_argv('Format <path>.py')` -> None, `door.solve('Format <file>.')` -> FAIL_CLOSED__STATED_SWE_EFFECT_UNSERVED in 56-181 ms with STATED_LINT_OR_FORMAT_NOT_PERFORMED_BY_CAPABILITY:UNNAMED, and 2 of the 4 formatter tests red on main. Under that, the write-authority rule refused the in-place rewrite itself (OUTPUT_OVERWRITES_A_STATED_SOURCE), because a destination that is also a source was refused without asking whether anything could CHECK the result. Now: a postcondition re-derives the promise from disk (`ruff format --check`, and the file must still parse), a rewrite the acceptance layer can judge is allowed through, and the typed-plan refusal asks the composer before it gives up. Door: PASS on a badly formatted file (rewritten and verified), FAIL_CLOSED__NO_OBSERVED_EFFECT on an already-formatted one.
